transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Sam Rodriguez (CTO, Acme); Lena Kim (ML Eng); Ravi Desai (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align success criteria for a POC comparing Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Discussed workload sizing, latency/cost tradeoffs, security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), and concrete benchmark plan + timelines. Agreed to run a SE-led benchmark and share pricing and SOW.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency P95, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy/regression thresholds)
- Workload sizing: peak qps, average seq length, concurrency, KV-cache hit assumptions
- Benchmarks: datasets, test harness, metrics, timeline
- Deployment decision criteria: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (security, latency, throughput, cost predictability)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call — I think Priya is with me, our SE, and on the customer side Sam, Lena, Ravi. sound good?
[00:15] Sam (Acme - CTO): Yeah hi, thanks Jordan. We got the calendar. Sorry ran over on another meeting but all good.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all — I'll mostly cover technical bits and the benchmark approach; Jordan will handle pricing and contract questions.
[00:30] Jordan: Super. High level from Acme side, what are your primary goals for the POC? Sam, do you want to kick off?
[00:38] Sam: Sure. We want to validate three things: one, latency — p95 under 300ms for short chat flows, two, cost — we need to understand unit economics at our expected scale, and three, quality/regression — no worse than 2% drop vs our current baseline on intent classification. We're also sensitive to data residency and SOC 2 type requirements.
[01:05] Lena: And from ML side, we have a mix — short messages like 16-64 tokens for chat assistants, and long-form summarization up to 1k tokens for docs. Our typical concurrency peaks around 200 concurrent requests, average seq length about 80, but long tails exist.
[01:27] Ravi: On infra, we need to know networking — whether we can do VPC peering for private, and what ports, plus whether KMS/HSM integrations are supported for key management. Also interested in audit logs and retention.
[01:45] Priya: Great — that's exactly the info we need to size the POC. We'll propose a benchmark that mirrors that mix: 70% short chat, 30% long-form, with synthetic traffic to simulate 200 concurrents and a burst profile.
[02:00] Jordan: Quick framing on deployment types: Hosted is fastest to get started — you hit our API, you get multi-tenant hosted infra; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower jitter; Private is a customer-managed control plane (VPC/on-prem) for strict compliance or air-gapped setups. We'll walk tradeoffs.
[02:22] Sam: When do you recommend Dedicated vs Private? Like, at what scale or requirement would we choose each?
[02:30] Priya: Good question. Dedicated is typically chosen when you need predictable latency and throughput — e.g., sustained high qps or strict latency SLOs — and you want cost predictability via a committed capacity. Private is chosen when you have regulatory constraints — data cannot leave your VPC or you need customer-managed KMS/HSM or on-prem. If you just need lower latency but are fine with Redwood managing infra, Dedicated often hits the sweet spot.
[02:55] Lena: What about performance tuning like quantization or batching?
[03:00] Priya: We support quantized model variants and automatic batching. For chat flows where latency matters, we tune for small batches and KV cache hits; for long-form, we can increase batch size and select a different kernel path. One note: quantization can change output slightly, so we include quality evals in the benchmark.
[03:20] Sam: That brings me to success criteria — the latency numbers are clear, cost per 1M tokens is a must, and for quality we need an evaluation suite. Can Redwood run that or do we provide prompts?
[03:35] Jordan: We can do both. Priya will run a Redwood SE-led benchmark using your prompts if you provide them, or we can use a shared eval set. Lena, can you share a sample prompts set?
[03:45] Lena: Yes, I'll upload 200 prompts covering intent/classification, summarization, and dialog. Expect that by Friday.
[03:52] Ravi: Network-wise, how do you handle private connectivity? Is it VPC peering or a private link?
[03:58] Priya: We support VPC peering and cloud interconnect in most regions; for Private, we can deploy an agent in customer VPC or run an on-prem package. We'll share network diagrams.
[04:10] Sam: Security — SOC 2 and SSO with SAML are must-haves. Also need audit logs and encryption at rest with our KMS.
[04:18] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO support, RBAC, and can integrate with your KMS for Private deployments. For hosted, we offer customer-specific key wrapping and audit logs. We'll attach our security pack.
[04:30] Priya: For the benchmark itself, high level plan: 1) baseline run on Hosted default model, 2) Dedicated run with committed GPU config, 3) Private run (if you want us to spin a private env) — compare p50/p95, token cost, throughput, and quality regression. We'll also test caching behavior — measure KV cache hit rates with warm vs cold states.
[04:55] Lena: How long do these runs take? We want results quickly to make a quarter planning decision.
[05:00] Priya: Each benchmark matrix (short chat profile + long-form profile) takes about 2 hours to run per deployment mode plus setup. So Hosted+Dedicated could be done in a day if we pre-provision; Private depends on provisioning window — might take a day or two. We'll aim to have results within a week if we start next week.
[05:20] Jordan: Timeline-wise we propose: share baseline prompts + traffic profile this week, Redwood runs Hosted baseline and shares results mid-next week, Dedicated estimate + pricing sent by Jordan by Friday, then schedule Dedicated benchmark for week of 9/21. Does that align?
[05:35] Sam: That works. We also need SOW and pricing to present to procurement.
[05:40] Jordan: I'll put together a draft SOW and committed capacity pricing options — 3-month pilot vs 12-month reserved — and send by 9/17.
[05:50] Ravi: On cost modeling — do you provide cost per 1M tokens for both hosted and dedicated? We want to compare hit-per-token unit economics plus overhead for VPC.
[05:58] Jordan: Yes. For Hosted we'll give usage-based numbers; for Dedicated we'll model committed GPU amortized cost and expected throughput to compute per-1M tokens. We'll include assumptions for batching and KV cache hit rates, so you can adjust.
[06:15] Priya: A few technical clarifications we should capture now: what are your expected batch sizes, typical prompt + response lengths, and do you have streaming requirements?
[06:25] Lena: Streaming for chat is a yes. Avg prompt 16 tokens, avg response 64 tokens for chat; for long-form doc summarization prompt 120 tokens, response 800-1200 tokens. Batch size typically small for chat — 1-4; long-form can batch up to 8-16.
[06:45] Priya: Perfect — that'll guide kernel selection and batching config. Also, do you expect high KV cache reuse? If users frequently re-prompt the same context, cache hits matter a lot for latency.
[06:55] Sam: We have medium cache reuse — maybe 40-50% on returning sessions. Provide numbers both for warm and cold cache.
[07:05] Priya: Will do. Regarding model variants — do you prefer a specific open checkpoint or do you want Redwood to recommend a profile?
[07:12] Lena: We tried an internal open model but are flexible; recommend what gives best cost/latency tradeoff.
[07:18] Priya: We'll recommend two variants: a quantized faster variant and a higher-precision variant for quality-sensitive flows, and include regression checks.
[07:25] Jordan: On legal/compliance, procurement will ask for data retention and deletion procedures — we'll include that in the security pack. Anything else?
[07:33] Ravi: Audit log retention length — we need 1 year. Also, encryption key rotation policy.
[07:38] Jordan: Noted — we'll confirm retention and rotation details in the security docs we send.
[07:45] Sam: For Dedicated capacity, what's the typical lead time to provision a reserved GPU pool?
[07:50] Priya: If we have available capacity in region, it can be hours to a day; if we need new hardware or different region, could be longer. For the POC we'll try to use existing pools.
[07:58] Sam: Ok. Another question — how do you handle graceful degradation / fallbacks? If a model fails, can you route to a cheaper model or another region?
[08:07] Priya: Yes — routing policies support fallback to compatible model variants or a lower-cost tier and region-based fallback. We can configure automatic fallback, canary rollout, and A/B tests. We'll demonstrate during the benchmark.
[08:20] Jordan: Let's talk acceptance criteria more concretely — propose we use: p95 latency < 300ms for short chat with warm cache, throughput sustain at 200 concurrent with <5% error rate, cost <= X per 1M tokens (we'll compute X once we have traffic), and quality regression <= 2% on your eval set. Agree?
[08:40] Sam: Yes that looks reasonable. For procurement, we'll also need a list of stakeholders and sign-off criteria — I'll share the procurement timeline.
[08:50] Lena: We'll also want to test model output variability — temperature and top-k effects. Can Redwood's test harness sweep those params?
[08:56] Priya: Yes, we can do parameter sweeps and capture metrics. We'll share the harness instructions.
[09:05] Jordan: Any blockers from your side to start?
[09:08] Sam: Not really; main blocker is access to prompts and a sampling of real traffic or a histogram. We'll get that to you.
[09:15] Ravi: Also need to confirm our security review window — procurement wants the security docs a week before contract.
[09:21] Jordan: We'll send the security pack ASAP, same with SOW draft.
[09:24] Priya: Ok next up, I'll run through a proposed benchmark matrix — quick table verbally: Mode / Profile / Duration / Metrics. Hosted-default: short-profile 2hr run, long-profile 2hr run; Dedicated: same; Private: optional. We'll collect p50/p95, throughput, errors, token cost, KV-cache hit rate, and quality diff.
[09:50] Lena: For the long-form runs, do you simulate storage or streaming? It's mainly batch.
[09:55] Priya: We'll simulate as a batch job with streaming disabled. For chat we'll enable streaming.
[10:02] Sam: When you compute cost per 1M tokens for Dedicated, will you include network egress or is that separate?
[10:08] Jordan: We'll include compute and infra amortized cost; network egress will be itemized separately since it depends on your cloud provider and peering.
[10:15] Ravi: For Private/on-prem, any extra licensing or infra fee?
[10:18] Jordan: Private has a platform fee plus support tier; we'll include a line item. For on-prem, there may be install and support hours.
[10:26] Priya: Small gotcha: quantized variants may show a small quality shift; we'll mark thresholds where quantization is acceptable. We'll include that in the regression tests.
[10:35] Sam: Great. Let's recap and confirm next steps.
[10:40] Jordan: Recap: Jordan sends SOW + pricing (due 9/17), Priya shares benchmark worksheet/test harness (due 9/16), Acme provides prompts and traffic hist (due 9/18), schedule benchmark week of 9/21. We'll aim to deliver Hosted baseline mid-next week. Action items captured.
[10:58] Sam: Sounds good. Any open questions?
[11:02] Lena: No, thanks — excited to see the results.
[11:05] Ravi: We'll look out for the security docs.
[11:08] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the security pack and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[11:15] Priya: Thanks all.
[11:18] Sam: Bye.
